problem: Eviction changed from a sliding window to fixed buckets (q[0] < bucket_start), so up to 2x limit requests are admitted across a bucket boundary and requests can be wrongly denied, contradicting SlidingWindowLimiter and the (now - window, now] semantics.
retry_after still computes q[0] + window - now (sliding expiry) while _in_window now evicts on bucket boundaries, so the hint disagrees with allow() and can be too long or too short.
Float floor division (now // window) misplaces bucket edges for float windows (0.3 // 0.1 == 2.0) and yields nan for now=inf, so nothing is evicted; the old subtraction cutoff was exact.

Inline __import__("collections").deque() ignores the existing deque import on line 2 and setdefault allocates a throwaway deque on every call; the comment documenting the window semantics was also deleted.
_accepted never drops keys, and remaining/retry_after create entries for unseen keys, so attacker-chosen keys grow memory without bound (pre-existing).
_observe stores _last_now before validating now, so a NaN or non-numeric first value poisons the limiter (pre-existing).
